dublinCore.title: FFT with Multiple Frequency Components
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal Processing
FFT
Superposition
Harmonic Analysis
dublinCore.description: Three sine-wave oscillators are added together and played. A triggered 20 ms window of the combined waveform is shown in the time domain and its FFT magnitude spectrum from 0 to 1600 Hz below, with a frequency label on each peak, so students can relate each component's frequency and amplitude to a spectral peak.
relation: Chapter 7: DFT, FFT and Frequency Domain Analysis

learningObjectives: Predict that setting the three frequency sliders to distinct values produces three separate peaks in the FFT spectrum at those frequencies
Explain how the complicated time-domain waveform arises from the superposition of three sine waves whose amplitudes are set by the amplitude sliders
Compare the height of each spectral peak to its oscillator's amplitude setting to relate FFT magnitude to component amplitude
Predict what happens to the spectrum when two oscillators are tuned to the same or nearly the same frequency, or when one amplitude is set to zero
Distinguish the time-domain plot, which shows amplitude against time, from the frequency-domain plot, which shows magnitude against frequency
prerequisites: Sine waves: frequency, period and amplitude
Basic FFT MicroSim (one sine wave gives one peak)

misconceptions.misconception: A complicated waveform must contain many frequencies
misconceptions.correction: Adding sine waves creates no new frequencies; the spectrum shows exactly one peak per component
misconceptions.evidence: 300, 600 and 900 Hz give exactly three peaks and nothing at sums such as 1500 Hz

misconceptions.misconception: Two tones always show up as two peaks, and equal tones add to a1 + a2
misconceptions.correction: The FFT has finite frequency resolution, and equal-frequency sines add like phasors
misconceptions.evidence: 400 Hz and 410 Hz merge into one pulsing peak; two 400 Hz tones of amplitude 0.5 give a single peak anywhere from 0 to 1.0 depending on their phase difference

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Three sine-wave oscillators are added together. The top plot shows the combined waveform over a 20 millisecond window; the bottom plot shows its FFT magnitude spectrum from 0 to 1600 Hz with a frequency label on each peak. Press Start, then move the frequency and amplitude sliders of each component.

visualElements.description: Time-domain plot (blue): a 20 ms window of the combined waveform, triggered on the steepest rising zero crossing; the amplitude axis is +/-1, +/-2 or +/-3 depending on a1 + a2 + a3
Frequency-domain plot (red bars): FFT magnitude spectrum from 0 to 1600 Hz with dark-red frequency labels on up to five peaks
Formula of the signal being played, slider read-outs, sample rate and bin width, and a STOPPED / PLAYING / MUTED status indicator

model.description: Three oscillators produce x(t) = a1 sin(2 pi f1 t) + a2 sin(2 pi f2 t) + a3 sin(2 pi f3 t). The browser's analyser (via p5.sound) applies a Blackman window and an 8192-point FFT returning 4096 bins; the sketch plots the magnitude normalised so that an amplitude-1 sine centred on a bin reaches 1. The Master gain sits between the oscillators and the speakers, after the FFT tap.
equations: x(t) = a1 sin(2 pi f1 t) + a2 sin(2 pi f2 t) + a3 sin(2 pi f3 t)
two equal-frequency tones: amplitude |a1 + a2 e^{j phi}|
algorithms: Local-maximum peak detection with label collision avoidance
Steepest rising zero-crossing trigger for the time-domain display
limitations: Labels report the centre of the strongest bin, up to half a bin (about 2.9 Hz at 48 kHz) from the true frequency
A tone between two bins reads up to about 12% low because of the Blackman window
Tones 10 Hz apart merge into one peak

instructionalStrategies: Comparing peak heights with amplitude settings
Finding the smallest frequency separation the FFT can resolve
extensions: Add a phase slider for each oscillator and show that the magnitude spectrum does not change
Compare FFT sizes to see how bin width changes the resolution limit
